title: Sales enablement prospect playbook — positioning, messaging, competitive briefs, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Jordan Alvarez
content:
Overview

This playbook is a single-page reference for Redwood Inference sellers and solution engineers who are engaging with prospects. It consolidates core positioning and messaging, competitor brief summaries, pitch-deck guidance, recommended pricing conversation flows, two short case studies, objection handling, and a concise security FAQ for prospect conversations. Use this during discovery calls, technical POCs, and procurement discussions.

One-liner

Redwood Inference: a production-first LLM inference platform that delivers predictable latency, lower unit costs, and unified operations across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Elevator pitch (30s)

- Problem: Teams struggle to run LLMs at production scale because of unpredictable latency, high per-token costs, and operational complexity.
- Solution: Redwood provides a high-throughput serving runtime, routing and cache optimizations, and deployment flexibility (hosted, dedicated, private) so engineering teams get predictable performance and economics with minimal ops overhead.
- Why it matters: Faster time-to-market for LLM features, lower ongoing inference spend, and fewer outages or regressions in production.

Core positioning pillars (talk tracks)

1) Production economics: predictable per-token unit cost and tooling to reduce spend (intelligent batching, caching, automatic fallbacks).
2) Performance and reliability: single-digit 95th-percentile latency for common configs, SLA-backed Dedicated tiers, multi-region fallbacks.
3) Developer-first: consistent API & SDKs, streaming, function calling, and clear performance expectations for different model families.
4) Flexible deployment: hosted for speed, Dedicated for capacity and isolation, Private (VPC / on-prem) for compliance.

Buyer personas & messaging (quick probes and tailored value)

- ML / ML Infra (primary technical buyer): focus on model fidelity, latency, cost per token, quantization options, and model on-call. Ask: "What are your p95 latency targets and typical sequence lengths?"
  - Message: Redwood reduces unit cost with KV/prefix caching, batching, and model quantization profiles while preserving quality via A/B rollouts.
- Platform / SRE: focus on SLA, autoscaling, observability, tracing. Ask: "How do you measure token-level cost and tail latency today?"
  - Message: Per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and auto-fallback policies reduce operational surprise.
- Product / Engineering PM: focus on features, release velocity, and reliability. Ask: "Which user-facing flows are latency-sensitive?"
  - Message: Start on Hosted to iterate fast, then move to Dedicated/Private for scale and compliance.
- Procurement / Finance: focus on predictable spend, committed discounts, and billing terms. Ask: "Do you prefer usage-based or committed spend models?"
  - Message: We offer usage-based billing for quick pilots and reserved capacity contracts for predictable unit economics.

Key proof points and metrics (shareable in pitch)

- Typical Hosted 95th percentile latency for chat workloads (seq_len=512): 80–250 ms (depends on model family and config).
- Customer examples: 35–55% reduction in per-token bill via caching + batching on retrieval-augmented generation workloads.
- SLA: Dedicated customers get 99.95% uptime and prioritized scheduling.
- Quantization & profiles: 8-bit and 4-bit quantization profiles with verified throughput improvements (2–4x) for recommended workloads.

Competitive brief (short table)

Competitor | Strengths | Weaknesses | Redwood positioning
---|---:|---|---
Cloud A (managed endpoints) | Deep cloud integrations, global regions | Higher per-token costs, less inference-specific optimizations | Better unit economics & inference-first optimizations; multi-deployment modes
Vendor B (open-source runtime) | Low license cost, community | Heavy ops burden, limited enterprise integrations | Offer managed Dedicated + Private with ops support and SLOs
LLM-API X (hosted API leader) | Simple API, large model catalog | Less predictable latency at scale, limited private deployment options | Unified runtime across hosted and private with clear rollback policies
On-prem integrators | Full control | Long delivery cycles, limited autoscaling | Faster POCs, autoscaling and fallbacks, and hybrid options

Sales plays and playbooks (how to structure an engagement)

1) Quick pilot (1–2 weeks): Hosted trial with sample dataset + test prompts. Deliverables: baseline latency/cost report, suggested quantization/batching configs, and recommended Dedicated footprint for production.
2) Technical POC (2–6 weeks): Dedicated or Private preview, workload-level benchmarking (latency percentiles, throughput), and failover tests. Deliverables: perf report, cost model, runbook for rollout.
3) Enterprise onboarding (4–12 weeks): Procurement, security review, capacity commitments, and production cutover with canary rollout. Deliverables: signed contract, onboarding plan, SLA definition, runbooks.

Pitch-deck outline (recommended slide sequence + notes)

1. Title & Value Proposition — Single-sentence impact for the buyer.
2. Customer problem — concrete examples of production pain (latency spikes, runaway costs, model regressions).
3. Redwood solution overview — runtime, smart routing, cache, deployments.
4. How it works at a high-level — diagram + one-sentence each: serving runtime, routing, caching, deployment abstraction.
5. Performance & economics — share example percentiles & cost delta (hosted pilot numbers).
6. Deployment options & security — Hosted, Dedicated, Private + compliance badges (SOC2, ISO, HIPAA as applicable).
7. Pricing models & example TCO — usage-tier example and reserved capacity math.
8. Case studies & results — two short customer stories with metrics.
9. POC plan & success criteria — timelines and gates.
10. Next steps & ask — contact, trial link, procurement checklist.

Pricing guidance (how to discuss numbers)

- Overview of models: 
  - Hosted: usage-based pricing (per 1K input tokens / per 1K output tokens or per-embedding unit). Ideal for pilots.
  - Dedicated: committed monthly/annual capacity with lower unit price and SLA. Ideal for predictable throughput.
  - Private: licensing + support fee for on-prem/VPC deployments (custom pricing).

- Negotiation rules of thumb:
  - For early-stage pilots keep discussion focused on value delivered (latency, customer experience) rather than raw token price; offer a 30–60 day trial with usage credits.
  - For enterprise deals, move to committed capacity quoting: show TCO models comparing Hosted vs Dedicated over 12 months (assume sample throughput and 20–40% discount on unit price for committed spend).
  - Add-ons: extended observability retention (+$X / month), premium SLA (+$Y / month), compliance package (audit log retention, legal review).

Example pricing conversation script (concise)

- If prospect asks about unit price: "For pilots we recommend Hosted — we'll provide trial credits and a short benchmark. If you expect predictable production throughput, Dedicated gives a 20–40% lower unit cost with SLA and capacity guarantees. We can model your expected QPS and latency to show the TCO differential."

Case studies (short, anonymized templates)

1) Fintech customer — Conversational support at scale
- Customer: mid-size fintech processing customer queries across mobile and web.
- Challenge: 500ms p95 target for chat, high costs from repeated long-context inference, frequent model updates.
- Approach: Hosted pilot -> Dedicated baseline -> implement KV caching + caching-layer for user context -> A/B rollout.
- Results: Reduced p95 latency from 620ms to 160ms for seq_len=512; 42% reduction in per-session inference cost after caching and batching; zero-seconds of downtime during rollout with canary fallbacks.

2) Retail search & recommendations (embeddings)
- Customer: large online retailer using embeddings for product search and personalization.
- Challenge: high embedding QPS with bursty traffic during promotions; need predictable throughput and regional controls.
- Approach: Dedicated cluster with autoscale policy and regional routing; warm KV cache for product catalog embeddings.
- Results: 3x throughput improvement with 25% lower cost per embedding call vs baseline; consistent tail latency under 200ms; simplified deployment via Dedicated contracts.

Objection handling (short bullets)

- "We already run models in-house": Acknowledge investment. Highlight Redwood's options for Private deployments and ops support that reduce integration time and add autoscaling, tracing, and runbooks.
- "Per-token price is too high": Validate current baseline, propose pilot to measure end-to-end unit economics (caching/batching effects), and offer committed discounts for Dedicated.
- "Security and compliance concerns": Point to Private deployment, KMS integrations, audit logs, and support for SOC2/HIPAA where applicable — then escalate to security team for detailed TAs.

Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers for first-touch conversations)

Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: For Hosted customers, data is stored in the customer’s geographic region where available; we support regional tenancy for EU and selected APAC regions. For Dedicated and Private, data is isolated to the customer’s VPC or on-prem environment.

Q: Do you use customer data to train models?
A: Redwood does not use customer request data to train public models. Customers can opt-in for aggregated telemetry used only to improve platform reliability; opt-in is explicit and documented in the contract.

Q: How are keys and secrets managed?
A: We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and offer HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. API keys are stored in an encrypted secrets store with RBAC.

Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 (summaries available). We support contractual commitments for HIPAA via BAAs for eligible customers and can provide compliance packages during procurement.

Q: Can we deploy in our VPC / on-prem?
A: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC deployments and an on-premise package for air-gapped environments. The Private offering includes a customer-managed control plane option for additional isolation.

Q: Is end-to-end encryption available in transit and at rest?
A: Yes. All network traffic uses TLS 1.2+ in transit. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256; keys are customer-managed when using Private deployments or Dedicated with KMS integration.

Q: How long do you retain logs and request data?
A: Default retention is 30 days for request logs in Hosted. Retention can be extended for Dedicated at an additional cost; Private deployments are fully customer-configurable. We provide deletion APIs and contractual data deletion commitments.

Q: Do you perform regular penetration tests and third-party audits?
A: Yes. We run annual third-party penetration tests and continuous vulnerability scanning. Summary reports are available under NDA during procurement.

POC / Technical checklist (items to validate during trial)

- Define success criteria: 95th percentile latency target, throughput target (QPS), cost per 1M tokens target, and acceptable model quality delta.
- Provide representative prompt set and sample traffic profile (seq_len distribution, QPS).
- Baseline measurements: existing latency and spend.
- Redwood deliverables: benchmarking report, recommended quantization profile, suggested Dedicated sizing and autoscale policy, and runbook for cutover.

Resources & next steps

- Recommended next step for reps: Schedule a technical discovery call with Solutions Engineering, request sample prompts and traffic profile, and enable a 14–30 day Hosted trial with benchmark deliverable.

Appendix: Common SLAs and performance targets (reference)

- Hosted: no formal uptime SLA; support response within 24 hours for trial accounts.
- Dedicated: 99.95% uptime SLA; accounted credits for downtime. Typical provisioned p95 latency targets: small-chat models 80–250ms, embeddings 40–150ms (workload dependent).
